# Labeled mixed-cap pyramids and exact threshold cancellation

This extends the actual pyramid bound in `candidate 600f7b09ccd06ced` to arbitrary positive compatible fibers, ambient oblique caps, and consistent inside/outside supporting allocations. The retained object is a fiber-labeled directed support integral, not a Blaschke body with the labels discarded. It supplies a sharp geometric lower bound and an exact nonnegative cap remainder. It does not supply a parity budget or a universal lower bound for that integral.

## 1. Coarea normalization and the all-status cone bound

Let P be finite, let K_z be positive compact convex d-bodies, and let

    H={a.z+u.X>=c},  u!=0,
    tau_z=c-a.z,    q_Hz=|K_z intersect H|.

Use the SAME allocated section measure lambda_Hz as the physical cap record. Its mass T_Hz has COAREA normalization: a proper section has measure dH^(d-1)/|u|. On an inside supporting facet its density is (1-s_H)/|u|; on an outside supporting facet its density is s_H/|u|. Here s_H is the actual body selector, with values in [0,1] on a coincident facet. Strict full/empty fibers have T_Hz=0. Set

    G_Hz=[h_Kz(u)-tau_z] T_Hz,
    D_Hz=d q_Hz-G_Hz.                              (1)

Then G_Hz>=0 and D_Hz>=0 in every status. In particular

    d Q_H=sum_z G_Hz+sum_z D_Hz,
    Q_H=sum_z q_Hz.                                (2)

There is no additional |u| in (1). Equivalently, for e=u/|u|, the term is

    [h_Kz(e)-tau_z/|u|] * (|u| T_Hz).

For a proper section F, choose a farthest captured point v of K_z. The actual pyramid conv(F,v) lies in K_z intersect H. Its volume is

    |F| [h_Kz(u)-tau_z]/(d |u|)=G_Hz/d.

At an inside supporting facet, the whole K_z is captured and the allocated area is at most |F|; the same pyramid inclusion bounds G_Hz/d by |K_z|. At an outside support the height is zero, so G_Hz=q_Hz=0 regardless of its selected area. Lower-dimensional touches have zero allocated (d-1)-measure. Strict full fibers contribute D_Hz=d|K_z|, and strict empty fibers contribute zero. This proves (1)--(2), including d=1 with endpoint counting.

For a partial supporting allocation, G_Hz/d can also be viewed as the weighted volume of the actual pyramid rays with the same section density. No replacement of its tangential allocation by a uniform smaller facet is needed. The remainder in (1) retains the allocation; it is not always the excess over the full unallocated pyramid.

For a pure-base cap set G_Hz=0 and D_Hz=d q_Hz. Its whole-fiber captured volume remains in (2).

If theta is a probability law of actual equal-mass caps Q_H=Q, integration yields the exact positive-remainder identity

    dQ=int_H sum_z [h_Kz(u)-c+a.z]T_Hz dtheta
                                      +int_H sum_z D_Hz dtheta. (3)

## 2. Exact cancellation and the hypotheses it actually needs

First consider one group with a reference mark Y=(p,y). No stationarity is presumed yet. Write

    T_H=sum_z T_Hz,
    b_H=sum_z T_Hz(z-p),
    delta_H=c-a.p-u.y,
    V=int_H T_H u dtheta.

Direct expansion gives

    int_H sum_z G_Hz dtheta
      =int_H sum_z h_Kz(u)T_Hz dtheta
         +int_H a.b_H dtheta-int_H delta_H T_H dtheta-y.V. (4)

Thus the sufficient exact cancellation premises are

    b_H=0 for theta-a.e. H,
    delta_H=0 for theta-a.e. H,
    int_H T_H u dtheta=0.                          (5)

Under (5),

    dQ=int_H sum_z h_Kz(u)T_Hz dtheta
                                      +int_H sum_z D_Hz dtheta. (6)

The support expression in (6) is translation-invariant by the last balance in (5), even if individual support values use an arbitrary origin. It is nonnegative because it equals the original nonnegative cone expression.

The first premise is the allocated BASE-section centroid condition for each cap; the second is its through-mark condition; the third is the actual group continuous-normal balance. Only having a group-averaged base mean is insufficient to cancel the cap-dependent a.b_H term. A centroid of every individual proper section must not be substituted for an allocated mixed mean.

A useful alternative sufficient premise is that EVERY cap's entire allocated mixed section has the SAME full mean Y, together with the last balance in (5). Indeed the section is supported on a.z+u.X=c, so averaging that equality gives c=a.p+u.y automatically. This alternative permits p to be noninteger. In the audited ordinary limiting group, Y is the kappa-weighted barycenter of its retained contact marks, not necessarily any one of those marks. Precisely this common-mean statement is proved in `candidate 714f69e684c396b1`, Section 5. Using it here makes no new claim about projected base-normal balance or a group cover after clamping.

For an actual regular cap at an own-proper minimizing source Y, first variation in its BASE tilt gives b_H=0: the derivative of captured mass in direction dot a, while keeping the cap through Y, is dot a.b_H. At a nonregular cap this argument requires the consistent allocated derivative/dual, not a freely chosen section selector. Equation (6) applies once those exact means and balances have been independently supplied.

If caps are buffered, or only approximate balances are known, (4) remains the correct identity. Dropping its last three terms is not justified by smallness of a physical buffer alone when coefficients can diverge. The bounded record argument in Section 4 gives the safe limiting version.

## 3. What actual compatibility adds: an unfavorable support deficit

Assume (5), T_H>0, and p is a base with a positive canonical fiber. Set lambda_Hz=T_Hz/T_H. Then its base mean is p and actual convex compatibility gives

    sum_z lambda_Hz K_z subset K_p.

Consequently the explicitly nonnegative support deficit is

    S_H=T_H h_Kp(u)-sum_z T_Hz h_Kz(u)>=0.           (7)

Combining (3)--(7), and retaining the through-y form, gives

    dQ=int_H T_H h_(K_p-y)(u) dtheta
                   -int_H S_H dtheta+int_H sum_z D_Hz dtheta. (8)

Equation (8) is a directed, labeled exact identity. The support deficit is SUBTRACTED. Compatibility therefore bounds the mixed cone term ABOVE by the own-fiber support term; it does not turn that own-fiber term into a lower bound for dQ. No general comparison between the two nonnegative quantities int S_H and int sum D_Hz is proved here.

This sign is not cosmetic. Take P={-1,0,1}, K_-=K_+=[-1/2,1/2]^d and

    K_0=[-1,1] times [-1/2,1/2]^(d-1).

The family is actual, centrally symmetric, and compatible; the origin is an actual deepest source by central symmetry. Give the two caps +/-X_1>=0 equal weights. Every section has area and coarea one, every allocated mixed section has mean zero, T_H=3, all caps have Q=2, and all balances in (5) hold. For either cap

    sum_z h_Kz(u)T_Hz=2,
    T_H h_K0(u)=3,
    S_H=1,
    sum_z D_Hz=2d-2.

Thus (8) is 2d=3-1+(2d-2). Already in d=1 it is FALSE that dQ is at least the own support expression 3. The higher-dimensional version isolates the same nonzero compatibility deficit. The example's cap law has W=1/2 almost everywhere, so it also satisfies the complete signed normal-convex ordinary boundary stress. It is not a bad minimum.

## 4. Supporting limits and cap-law compactification

The identity is stable under the ACTUAL joint cap/section compactification. Suppose K_z^m converge to positive K_z in Hausdorff distance, all bodies remain bounded, and continuous cap normals satisfy 0<u_min<=|u|<=u_max. Retain bounded cap records (a,u,c), joint allocated section measures, and cap weights as in `candidate 714f69e684c396b1`.

Then h_Kz^m(u) converges uniformly on the compact normal set. The integrand h_Kz^m(u)-c+a.z is continuous and uniformly bounded on the joint section-record space. Weak convergence of the joint section measures therefore passes its integral exactly. Captured d-volumes also converge, since each nonzero continuous normal has a volume-null hyperplane. Thus the integrated D remainder converges and stays nonnegative.

This uses the actual limiting allocations: a proper cut may limit to an inside supporting facet with a positive section allocation, or to an outside supporting facet of zero captured volume. Replacing the limiting allocation by a new inside-zero convention would generally change (3).

The trace-preserving base clamp leaves every threshold tau_z EXACT on fibers carrying section mass, and hence preserves each G_Hz, T_Hz, section moment and cap volume. It need not preserve a projected sum of base normals. The safe cancellation route after passing to bounded records is the common full section mean and continuous-normal balance in Section 2; these survive in the stated audited group limit. No unbounded product a.b_H is passed on the strength of separate weak limits.

## 5. Comparison with the available scalar and facet credits

For a single body with sections through its source, (6) reduces to

    beta |B| >= V(B,(-J)[d-1]),

where S_J is the oriented section measure. The simplex calibration is exact: this mixed-volume term is Gamma_d|B|, whereas the angularly averaged cap-shadow lower bound retains only Gamma_d|B|/d. The directed cone inequality therefore retains more scalar information on that calibration. The anisotropic cube instead gives the same term |B|/(2d), and the exact positive remainder is (d-1)|B|/(2d); no universal Gamma lower bound for the cone term is possible.

The harmonic contact-facet credit in `candidate 101249feac4a4158` concerns a simultaneously realizable first variation at a Minkowski midpoint and SAME-cap endpoint traces. The present identities concern existing cap VOLUMES, cut-section areas and far support heights. Neither theorem contains the other: this calculation needs no shared normal fan or realizable facet motion, but it gives no first-variation loss ratio. Equation (8) explicitly identifies the geometric deficit that prevents silently promoting it to an own-source or parity-efficient payment.

The supporting allocations can weaken the cone term even at fixed actual critical caps. For the three identical cubes at P={-1,0,1}, take the opposite caps +/-[(1/2)z+X_1]>=0. They have Q=3/2 and opposite selectors summing to one. At each endpoint supporting facet choose the same section fraction gamma in [0,1]; the central section is fully allocated. All mixed section means and balances in (5) hold. For either cap

    T_H=1+2 gamma,
    sum_z G_Hz=1/2+gamma,
    sum_z D_Hz=3d/2-1/2-gamma.

The outside endpoint pays no cone height, while the inside endpoint contributes gamma. These are genuine consistent allocations and actual global critical caps. They illustrate why the same allocated records, rather than arbitrary full sections, must be retained.

The companion checker is `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_labeled_mixed_cap_pyramids_slab_recovery.py`. Its exact checks cover proper, inside, outside and pure-base statuses, the threshold-defect identity, common-mean cancellation, both actual cube families, and a proper-to-supporting limiting calibration. They supplement the geometric proof; they do not infer it from samples.
